stem: How did this ruling affect black people in the United States before the Civil War?

options.label: A
options.text: It gave free blacks a route to citizenship but denied that right to enslaved people.

options.label: B
options.text: It denied rights for enslaved people but allowed free blacks the right to sue.

options.label: C
options.text: It restricted enslaved people and free blacks from having a voice in federal courts.

options.label: D
options.text: It gave enslaved people and free blacks their freedom in the United States.

visual_elements:
A free negro of the African race, whose ancestors were brought to this country and sold as slaves, is not a “citizen” within the meaning of the Constitution of the United States. . . .  
. . . Consequently, the special rights and immunities [guaranteed] to citizens do not apply to them. And not being “citizens” within the meaning of the Constitution, they are not entitled to sue in that character in a court of the United States.  
—Dred Scott v. Sandford
